::: {#thm-subset-intersection}
#### A subset is its own intersection

Let $A$ and $B$ be sets.
Then $A \subseteq B$ if and only if $A \cap B = A$.

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

($\Rightarrow$)
Suppose $A \subseteq B$.
We show $A \cap B = A$ with @thm-double-inclusion.
If $x \in A \cap B$, then $x \in A$ (@def-intersection).
If $x \in A$, then $x \in B$, since $A \subseteq B$,
so $x \in A \cap B$.

($\Leftarrow$)
Suppose $A \cap B = A$, and let $x \in A$.
Then $x \in A \cap B$, since the two sets are equal,
so $x \in B$.
So $A \subseteq B$.

:::

:::
